item.title: The more you work, the more you stay: the Ticino laps reform
item.description: The League calls for a reform of the laps with temporary incentives to work to eliminate the “poverty trap” and combat the impact of the LAMal awards.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The Ticino League calls for a reform of the laps with temporary work incentives - Objective: eliminate the "poverty trap" where increasing wages reduces benefits - Model already tested in social assistance: supplement of CHF 300 for those who reach 100% activation
## Key facts - **What**: Motion to reform the Law on Harmonization and Coordination of Social Benefits (laps) - When: Recently presented at the Grand Council - Where: Bellinzona, Ticino - Who: Grand Councillors Stefano Tonini and Alessandro Mazzoleni (and co-signatories) - Amount: Up to CHF 300 per month supplement for 100% job activation
A motion by the Ticino League proposes a profound reform of the laps to strengthen incentives to work and promote the economic autonomy of the beneficiaries. The proposal, presented by the great directors Stefano Tonini and Alessandro Mazzoleni and co-signed by Raffaella Zucchetti, Omar Balli, Sem Genini and Stefano Quadri, starts from a concrete observation: the increase in the cost of living and, above all, in health insurance premiums ([LAMal/KVG](nav:health)) are increasingly eroding the disposable income of Ticino's domestic economies.
The motioners recognise the essential role of cantonal social benefits, but call on the system to give higher priority to work, vocational reintegration and economic autonomy than a lasting dependence on state aid.
### The ### Concrete implications for beneficiaries and migration law
The proposed additional incentive should not constitute a new permanent benefit, but rather a time-limited promotional component. For this reason, the movers request that, to the maximum extent permitted by higher law, it be reserved for Swiss citizens and foreigners holding a residence permit C.
This choice has implications for the group of beneficiaries: the State Council will have to find a legally sustainable solution, taking into account the different situations of EU/EFTA citizens, third-country nationals, and other statuses protected by federal or international law. This is not a purely administrative matter, but one of compliance with Swiss migration law.
### AFI and API: a new legal qualification
A second chapter of the proposal concerns the supplementary allowance (AFI) and the early childhood allowance (API). The signatories request a review of their regulations so that they are configured as social benefits for economic support linked to need and subsidiarity, and when reasonably required, activation towards autonomy, rather than as family promotion measures.
This is a delicate move. Federal case law, particularly the DTF 141 II 401 decision, has qualified AFI and API as family policy instruments, excluding them from constituting social aid under migration law for this very reason. DTF 143 I 1 has also reconstructed the origin and family purposes of the benefits and examined the different access conditions provided for Swiss citizens and foreigners.
For the movers, any new qualification could not be limited to a simple change of name, but would require substantial changes to the purpose, structure, and conditions of the benefits. In other words: if AFI and API were to become social benefits for need-based support (rather than family benefits), the consequences for access rights and activation obligations would be significant.
True family promotion measures — those that go beyond covering an economic need and pursue objectives such as supporting the family, birth rates, and the reconciliation of family and professional life — should instead be regulated separately. On this point, the motion invites a resumption of the debate initiated in 2024 by the "Poker of initiatives to boost birth rates in Ticino" by the Gruppo il Centro + GdC.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### What changes for those receiving social benefits
If the motion is approved by the Grand Council and subsequently implemented by the State Council, LAPS benefit recipients will be able to count on stronger incentives when they increase their work activity. Instead of losing franc for franc the help they received, they will have access to an additional franchise, financial incentives, and reimbursement of expenses directly related to work.
In practice, the choice to move from a 40% job to a 60% job would become concretely advantageous, as the net (salary + incentives - reduction in aid) would be significantly positive.
### How to monitor and act
Those currently receiving social benefits in Ticino should: 1. Check the text of the motion when it is voted on in the Grand Council (normally on the parliamentary transparency portals of Ticino) 2. Contact the AI Office (Integrated Assistance) or the cantonal social service for clarifications on the times and methods of implementation 3. Concretely evaluate whether increasing the degree of employment is convenient, once the details of the incentives are known
Those currently unemployed or underemployed and who may be entitled to LAPS should monitor the evolution of the reform: if it passes, it could become economically sensible to seek more hours of work.
### Understanding the context of LAMal premiums
The motion itself starts from a crucial premise: the premiums of the health insurance (LAMal/KVG) are eroding the available income of Ticino families. This is a relevant national data point: LAMal premiums vary by canton and age class, and the Canton of Ticino provides cantonal subsidies to reduce the burden on low-income beneficiaries.
Consult the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) to understand how your gross income is transformed into net after taxes, pension contributions (AVS/AI/IPG, LPP), and, crucially, after the share you will pay for the LAMal premium. Understanding this impact is the first step to understanding whether an increase in employment (and LAPS incentives) is convenient for you.
Also monitor the [cost of living in Switzerland](nav:cost-of-living) to understand how inflation and the high cost of living influence your real budget, regardless of the number of hours worked.
### Next steps
The motion will have to be debated and voted on by the Ticino Grand Council. If approved, the State Council will have the mandate to develop a reform proposal for LAPS that incorporates the indicated principles: temporary incentives, additional franchises, linkage between increased work and concrete benefits.
The exact timeline is not yet clear, but it is likely that any implementations will begin from 2026 or 2027. Stay updated by consulting the official channels of the Canton of Ticino and the Grand Council.

item.title: Permit L Zurich: validity, renewal and extension
item.description: Permit L: maximum duration of one year, renewable if the contract continues. Transition to permit B and employer constraints in the Canton of Zurich.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Permit L: validity **maximum of 1 year** from issuance - Renewable if the employment contract continues with the same employer - Tied to the employer: job change requires administrative modification - Possible transition to Permit B (renewable residence) after 1–2 years
## Key facts - What: Short-term Permit L for fixed-term employment contract in Switzerland - Duration: Up to 12 months from the date of issuance by the SEM - Where: Managed by the SEM at the federal level; renewals coordinated by the cantons - Who: Non-EU/EFTA citizens and some EU citizens with a fixed-term contract - Tie: Associated with a specific employer named in the permit
The short-term Permit L is the entry document for those wishing to work in Switzerland with a fixed-term contract. It has a maximum validity of one year from issuance and is not automatically renewable: renewal depends on the continuity of the employment relationship and the assessment of the competent cantonal administration.
### What is Permit L Permit L is one of the categories of foreign permits (SEM) managed by the Central Information System on Migration. It differs from permanent permits: Permit B allows renewable residence, Permit C allows stable domicile (normally after 10 years of residence, or 5 years for EU/EFTA citizens).
Regarding access to the Swiss labor market, the holder of Permit L can only work for the employer specified in the initial application — there is a tie to the employer which is one of the differentiating factors compared to those who hold a Permit B. This means that a change of employer requires a modification of the documentation with the canton of residence.
In addition to the permit, every worker in Switzerland must take out [compulsory health insurance (LAMal)](nav:health) within 3 months of arrival. The mandatory contributions to be borne by the employee include AVS/AI/IPG (5.3% of salary) and LAINF/LAA (0.7–1.5% depending on the sector). ### Duration and Expiration of Permit L
The Permit L is valid for **up to 1 year** from the date of issuance. The canton and the SEM do not issue Permit L for different durations: the maximum is set at 12 months. This does not automatically mean that the permit cannot be renewed, but that the initial issuance has an annual validity. At the end, if the employment contract continues and the employer requests an extension (submitting an updated contract), the administration evaluates whether to renew the same Permit L or to transition the worker to Permit B.
The competent canton is normally the one where the worker resides. In the case of the Canton of Zurich, it is the Migration Office of the Zurich Cantonal Police that manages renewals and modifications after the initial issuance by the SEM.
### Scenarios of Extension and Renewal
Scenario 1: Renewal of the Same Permit L
The employer communicates to the canton that the contract continues. If there are no significant changes (same position, same salary, same location), the canton can renew the Permit L for an additional year. This can happen as long as the employer intends to maintain the employment relationship. There is no theoretical maximum limit on subsequent renewals, but each renewal is evaluated individually and lasts up to 1 year.
Scenario 2: Transition to Permit B
After 1–2 years of stable employment with Permit L, the employer and the worker can decide together to request conversion to Permit B (renewable residence). This is a natural step for those who intend to stay in Switzerland for a longer period and is associated with greater administrative stability. Permit B has an initial validity of 5 years and is renewable thereafter.
The transition from L to B is conditioned on: continuity of at least 1–2 years of employment, economic stability of the relationship, and positive evaluation by the cantonal administration.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Renewal procedure and required documents
To renew the L permit upon expiration, the procedure is as follows:
1. **Document collection**: the employer prepares an updated employment contract (or confirmation of the existing contract), salary statement, and certification of contributions [AVS/AI/IPG](nav:pension) (5.3% charged to the employee, 10.6% total with the employer) paid during the first year.
2. Request to the canton: 3–4 weeks before the L permit expires, the employer submits the renewal request to the Migration Office of the Zurich Cantonal Police (often through the canton's online portal).
3. Evaluation: the canton verifies that the contract is still in effect, that there are no defaults in mandatory contributions, and that the worker is compliant with federal, cantonal, and municipal taxes.
4. Issuance: if everything is in order, the canton coordinates the issuance of a new L permit with a maximum validity of 1 year.
⚠️ Attention: If the renewal request is not submitted before the expiration date, the worker loses their legal status to work in Switzerland. Even a few days of delay can result in significant consequences (sanctions for the employer, obligation to pay unpaid contributions, risk of repatriation). It is crucial to coordinate deadlines with the employer and the canton well in advance.
### Constraints related to the employer
One of the main constraints of the L permit is the association with a specific employer. Unlike the B or C permit, the holder of an L permit can only work for the employer named in the permit, cannot change employment without administrative modification with the canton, and cannot engage in self-employment without new federal authorization.
If the worker intends to change employers before the permit expires, they must notify the canton and the SEM. The new employer must submit a new work authorization request (work permit), which is evaluated with priority criteria for Swiss and European workers. The Federal Council has officially opened the consultation on the Agricultural Policy from 2030 (PA30+), with a deadline set for December 8. The reform revolves around a central objective: to expand the margin of maneuver for farmers to strengthen Switzerland's food security. This is a rewrite of the rules that will affect the entire agri-food chain, from producers to consumers.
The Executive emphasizes that it is not just the responsibility of farmers. PA30+ actively involves other actors in the agri-food chain and consumers themselves, who will have to take on greater responsibilities to ensure a sustainable food system from an ecological, economic, and social point of view. The reform develops along four strategic axes.
The first area concerns direct payments on ecology and animal welfare. The Federal Council revolutionizes the mechanism of contributions, orienting them towards concrete results rather than strict compliance with regulatory prescriptions. Digitalization plays a crucial role in reducing the administrative burden throughout the chain. A new legal basis will support these changes.
The second area focuses on market functioning. The Executive intends to strengthen market observation and extend solidarity measures. Additional support is planned for the dairy sector and for vegetable crops intended for human consumption—two pillars of Swiss production.
The third area concerns crop protection. Here the focus is on measures that promote beneficial insects and organisms, the use of sustainable technologies, and the strengthening of training and advice to farmers. A relevant aspect concerns the adaptation of farms to climate change, a theme increasingly urgent for the economic viability of crops.
The fourth area involves retail trade and consumers. The Government wants to promote sustainability through agreements on objectives with traders and greater awareness of Swiss products.

### Federal press release of September 2, 2026
Berne, September 2, 2026 — The Federal Council has officially launched the consultation on agricultural policy starting from 2030, named PA30+, with the declared objective of strengthening Switzerland's food security. The consultation remains open until December 8, 2026 and welcomes contributions from farmers, sector organizations, cantonal administrations, and citizens.
With this structural reform, the federal executive intends to expand the entrepreneurial margin of maneuver for Swiss farmers, strengthen added value creation and the efficiency of natural resources. At the same time, the government assigns greater responsibilities to the entire agri-food chain — from the food processing sectors, retail trade, to consumers — to ensure an ecologically, economically, and socially sustainable food system.
### Financial dimension of PA30+
The Federal Council has proposed to Parliament the spending limits for agriculture for the years 2030–2033 amounting to CHF 13.808 billion. This amount is lower by CHF 123 million compared to the financial allocation provided for the years 2026–2029, but exceeds by CHF 80 million the amount that would be maintained by keeping the 2030 financial plan in nominal terms. Parliament will still have to approve these spending limits in the next phase.
### The four strategic areas of PA30+
The Federal Council proposes specific measures articulated on four strategic axes. First, to expand the margin of maneuver and reduce administrative expenditure: currently, direct payments for ecology and animal welfare are strictly tied to the respect of specific prescriptions. PA30+ aims to reorient them towards the achievement of concrete results, giving farmers greater managerial freedom. The digitization of the entire chain will further reduce the administrative burden through a new legal basis that ensures simple and secure data exchange. ### How PA30+ transforms the relationship between farmers, markets, and consumers
The reform introduces a paradigm shift that involves all levels of the Swiss food chain, from agricultural enterprises to the consumer's table.
### Supporting markets and improving economic position
The second area of PA30+ aims to strengthen market observation and extend solidarity measures among operators to support agricultural enterprises in the valorization of their products. Additional financial support is explicitly provided for the dairy and vegetable crops sectors intended for direct human consumption. These measures directly contribute to improving the economic situation of farmers and strengthening their contractual position vis-à-vis distributors.
For those in the agricultural and food processing sectors, this means less market price volatility and better negotiation capacity with large distributors. For Swiss consumers, it translates into greater availability of quality local products, with direct implications for the national [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living).
### Investment in production bases and sustainable technologies
The third strategic axis addresses the structural foundations of Swiss food security: crop protection, promotion of beneficial insects and organisms, support for sustainable technologies, training, and specialized technical advice. These measures also support agricultural enterprises in adapting to climate change, a factor increasingly critical for the stability of Swiss food production.
Compared to the previous phase (2026-2029), the emphasis on resource efficiency and innovative technologies represents an important qualitative leap. It is no longer just about regulatory compliance but a structural modernization strategy for the Swiss primary sector, as desired by the Federal Council.
### Involvement of the supply chain and collective responsibility
The fourth area promotes sustainability throughout the agro-food value chain. Agreements on objectives between the Federal Council and the retail trade are planned, accompanied by initiatives to raise consumer awareness of a balanced diet based on quality Swiss products. PA30+ recognizes that food security is not the sole responsibility of farmers but must be shared by the entire supply chain, from processing to trade, to final consumers. item.title: AVS and complementary services in the canton of Aargau
item.description: First pillar of Swiss social security: AHV pension, calculation on contributory history, contributory gaps and supplementary benefits for minimum subsistence.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The AVS pension is the first pillar of Swiss social security - Contribution gaps reduce the amount of the annuity - Complementary benefits fill the gap between annuity and minimum subsistence
## Key facts - **What**: AVS System (Old Age and Survivors Insurance) - Who: UFAS/BSV oversees social security in Switzerland - When: Contributions paid throughout the working career - Where: Each canton (including Aargau) has a compensation fund - Amount: Income calculated on contribution history; supplementary benefits supplement
The first pillar of Swiss social security, managed by the UFAS/BSV (Federal Office of Social Insurance), is based on a mechanism of contributions paid during the entire working career. Each canton, including the canton of Aargau, has a cantonal compensation fund that administers these contributions and determines the amount of the AVS pension.
### How the AVS annuity is calculated
The AVS pension is not fixed: it depends directly on the number of years of contribution paid to the system. Each working year contributes to the final calculation of the service. Those who have paid contributions for their entire career receive the maximum amount; those who have contribution gaps receive a reduced income.
Contribution gaps may result from: - Unemployment periods not covered - Years in which the contribution has not been paid for administrative reasons - Move between cantons without ### Calculation of the pension and effects of gaps
The procedure for calculating the AVS pension follows a uniform national scheme, although it is administered at the cantonal level. The UFAS/BSV defines the parameters; the cantonal compensation fund of Aargau (like any other) applies the formulas to individual cases. To obtain an approximate simulation, you can use the [pension calculator](nav:calculator) available online.
A full year of contributions paid corresponds to one year of contribution. Are there missing contributions? Each missing year proportionally reduces the final pension. Someone who has paid 42 years of contributions out of 45 years of working life will have a reduction in the final pension.
There are mechanisms for filling gaps: it is possible to voluntarily pay back contributions, but within certain deadlines and limits set by law. Not all missing years can be recovered; the system provides well-defined deadlines.
### Supplementary benefits and minimum living standard
Supplementary benefits come into play when the combination of: - AVS pension - Income from other sources (possibly) - Movable/immovable assets
does not reach the minimum threshold set by cantonal law (with federal guidelines). The cantonal compensation fund processes the application and verifies the right.
The amount of the supplementary benefit is the difference between the recognized minimum living standard and the AVS pension received. It is not a fixed contribution but calculated case by case based on the economic situation.
### Difference between supplementary benefits and other subsidies
Do not confuse supplementary benefits (PC) with municipal social assistance, which is a different tool for protecting low incomes. PC are specifically linked to old age and insufficient AVS survivors; social assistance is generic and available for other population groups.
The cantonal compensation fund provides advice on this distinction during the processing of a PC application.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to verify your contribution history
The first step is to request an extract of your contribution history from the cantonal compensation fund of the canton of Aargau (or the canton of your current residence, if you have moved). This extract indicates: - Number of years of contributions paid - Recognized gap years - Amount of pension calculated at the time of request
You can obtain the extract by visiting in person, by mail, or through the online portal of the fund (where available). Many funds offer digital services to view your personal file in real-time.
### Procedure to request supplementary benefits
If the extract shows a low pension or if you know that you will live on an insufficient pension, you can apply for supplementary benefits:
1. Gather documents: copy of the AVS pension decision, income statement, bank statement, real estate ownership certificate (if owner).
2. Fill out the PC application form provided by the cantonal compensation fund.
3. Submit the application to the fund (by mail, email, or counter).
4. Wait for the review; the fund will assess the need according to the established legal criteria.
### Terms and deadlines
Supplementary benefits start from the month following the submission of the application (not retroactive, except for specific exceptions). It is advisable to submit the application before retirement or immediately after receiving the AVS pension decision, to avoid losing months of coverage.
The cantonal compensation fund remains available for telephone consultation, by email, or through a physical counter. Official websites and helplines provide updated information on forms and deadlines.

item.title: Teacher Shortage: A Report Analyzes Causes and Databases
item.description: The Federal Council approved the report on data collection and assessments concerning teacher shortages.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Federal Council approves report on teacher shortage - Report based on UST data up to 2034 - Multiple causes and regional differences - School reforms do not increase fluctuation
## Key facts - **What**: Report on data collection and evaluations concerning the teacher shortage - When: September 2, 2026 - Where: Bern - Who: Federal Council - Amount: Not specified
The Federal Council approved on September 2, 2026, the report on data collection and evaluations concerning the teacher shortage. The report shows that the phenomenon is due to several factors and that today there is already a solid data base for monitoring and for the measures to be taken, the competence for which lies with the Cantons. The report was drawn up in fulfillment of the postulates 22.4265 and 22.4266 of the Commission for Science, Education and Culture of the National Council (CSEC-N), with which it was requested to shed light on the causes of the teacher shortage and the reasons that lead to staying in or leaving the profession. The report was also to evaluate the school reforms carried out at the national level and the consequences in terms of additional burdens for teachers in a complete and systematic manner.
### Data and analysis The report is based on the statistical data of the Federal Statistical Office (UST) and, more precisely, on the statistics on school personnel, longitudinal analyses and scenarios on the need for teachers up to 2034. In addition, scientific studies and contributions from the Conference of Cantonal Directors of Public Education (CDPE) were also consulted. The teacher shortage is due to various causes, such as demographic trends, the peculiarities of the profession, specific factors related to the school environment, personal situation and needs related to a particular phase of life: these are the conclusions of the Federal Council's report. Statistical analyses generally show both a high stability of the profession and the fact that teachers often do not leave definitively, but rejoin the teaching staff at a later time.
According to the UST scenarios updated for the period 2025-2034, the need for teachers should change in the medium term. The decline in births will result in a lower number of entries into primary school from around 2027, and thus a lower need for new teachers. However, regional differences remain, which require foresight from the Cantons in school and personnel planning. ### Practical implications For the evaluation of school reforms, given the federal distribution of competencies, there can be neither national school reforms promoted by the Confederation nor federal evaluations of these reforms for the entire Switzerland. Reforms are coordinated and possibly evaluated at the cantonal or linguistic region level. The consulted research also shows that reforms alone do not lead to greater teacher fluctuation: for teachers, an additional burden is created, especially when new requirements do not provide adequate support or sufficient explanations regarding skills.
The report concludes that, at the national level, there is already a solid data base for monitoring teacher shortages and for the adoption of cantonal measures. Personal reasons for resignations and perceived overload only emerge to a limited extent from administrative data. Collecting this type of information is primarily the responsibility of the cantons. The Confederation plays a supportive role, particularly in providing reliable data and exchanging knowledge and best practices.
### Comparison with the previous situation Before the approval of this report, the cantons had difficulty planning school personnel due to the lack of reliable data and a long-term vision. With the availability of this new data, the cantons will be able to adopt more targeted and effective measures to address teacher shortages. This improvement in planning could lead to greater stability in school personnel and better quality of education.

This could include training new teachers, offering incentives to stay in the profession, and creating a more supportive work environment. The Confederation will continue to support the Cantons by providing reliable data and promoting the exchange of good practices.

item.description: The Federal Council proposes to allow the collecting institute LPP to deposit funds with the Confederation in the event of low or negative rates.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Federal Council has submitted the message to Parliament on the LPP. - The LPP collecting institution will be able to invest funds with the Confederation. - The measure applies in contexts of low or negative interest rates. - The validity of the legislative amendment will be limited to six years.
## Key facts - **What**: Investment of vested benefits funds with the Federal Treasury. - When: Message submitted on September 2, 2026. - Where: Bern, Switzerland. - Who: Federal Council and LPP collecting institution. - Condition: SNB policy rate equal to or less than 0 percent and coverage less than 103 percent.
On September 2, 2026, the Federal Council took note of the results of the consultation on the amendment of the Federal Law on Occupational Old-Age, Survivors' and Disability Pension Provision (LPP), submitting the relevant message to Parliament. The initiative aims to allow the LPP collecting institution to deposit vested benefits funds with the Federal Treasury, operating in conditions of absence of interest. This option is strictly linked to specific market scenarios, particularly when the policy rate of the Swiss National Bank is at levels equal to or less than zero percent. The primary objective of this regulation is to offer a risk management strategy in a financial context characterized by low or negative interest rates, while ensuring the stability of the institution.
### The role of the LPP collecting institution The LPP collecting institution, a foundation managed by the social partners, plays a fundamental role in the Swiss pension system. It has the obligation to accept the vested benefits funds of all those insured who, following the termination of their employment relationship and in the absence of a new affiliation, find themselves having to manage their pension position. To guarantee the nominal value of such assets, the institution is required to invest the capital in financial markets. However, the intrinsic volatility of such markets and the uncertainty related to the evolution of interest rates make access to risk-free deposit forms necessary. Historically, this possibility has already been exploited between May 2022 and March 2023, demonstrating the usefulness of this option to reduce the risk of insufficient coverage. The new legislative amendment, the validity of which will be limited to six years, represents an extension and consolidation of a mechanism already authorized by Parliament in September 2020. Managing occupational pension schemes in Switzerland requires extremely robust capital protection tools, especially during phases of economic instability. The option granted to the LPP substitute occupational benefit institution to deposit its assets with the Federal Treasury acts as a sort of financial parachute. This is not speculative management, but rather a defensive measure aimed at protecting the nominal value of vested benefit assets which, by law, must not suffer losses. When financial markets experience high volatility or negative returns, resorting to the Confederation prevents the institution's coverage ratio from falling below the critical threshold, in this case set at 103 percent. This approach reflects the need to balance the prudence required by occupational pension schemes with the dynamics of a market that, cyclically, can offer extremely low interest rates.
### Comparison between past and future The system has already been tested in the past, when Parliament had authorized this operation due to negative interest rates. The current procedure, which will expire in September 2027 regarding the previous regulation, is now being integrated and renewed through the Federal Council's new dispatch. The substantial difference lies in the structuring of a more solid and lasting legal basis, planned for a duration of six years. The public consultation highlighted broad consensus, with 36 out of 38 participants in favor of the project as a whole. This cross-party support confirms the perception of the instrument's validity among stakeholders. For anyone managing their [pension](nav:pension) or their pension assets, the stability of the substitute institution is a fundamental security factor. In a market where the cost-of-living and inflationary dynamics influence purchasing power, knowing that pension institutions have access to capital protection tools free from speculative risks represents a guarantee of solidity for the entire national pension system.

The management of vested benefits is a crucial aspect for every worker in Switzerland. When an employment relationship is terminated and no immediate new affiliation is made, the funds must be transferred to a vested benefits account or policy. The choice of the institution in which to deposit such sums is a personal decision that requires careful evaluation of the manager's solidity and investment strategies. Although the collecting LPP institution is the default option for those who do not have a new pension institution, it is useful to periodically monitor one's pension situation. item.title: Residence permit B Aargau: requirements and renewal
item.description: Permit B is the renewable residence in Switzerland. Federal SEM procedure, cantonal office competence. Complete guide to requirements, renewal and deadlines.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Permit B allows renewable residence in Switzerland for foreigners - Federal management through SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) - Renewal: cantonal migration office before expiration - Documents and duration remain at cantonal/federal level
## Key facts - **What**: Permit B, renewable residence authorization for foreigners - Who: Foreigners residing and working legally in Switzerland - Where: Federal competence SEM, procedure at the canton (Aargau) - Validity: Determined period, renewable upon request to the canton - Reference: Federal law on migration, art. foreign permits
The residence permit B is the authorization that allows a foreigner to reside in Switzerland for a limited period. Unlike the permit L (short duration, maximum 1 year), the permit B is renewable and is issued to those who intend to establish a more lasting residence in the country. The permit C, on the other hand, represents permanent residence and is usually granted after 10 years of continuous residence (or 5 years for citizens of the European Union or the European Free Trade Association).
The management of foreign permits in Switzerland falls under the competence of the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM), which operates at the federal level. However, the concrete procedure for renewing the permit B in the Canton of Aargau takes place at the competent cantonal migration office. Each canton organizes its own offices and the related administrative procedures, although the regulatory framework remains federal.
The permit B should not be confused with the permit G, which is reserved for cross-border commuters who work in Switzerland but do not reside there. Those arriving in the Canton of Aargau with the intention of residing and working will need a permit B (or L if the stay is very short), not a cross-border commuter permit.
The application for renewal of the permit B must be submitted to the migration office of the canton before the expiration of the current permit. The times and documents required for renewal are the responsibility of the Aargau cantonal administration and should be verified directly with the competent authority, as they vary from canton to canton. ### The B permit cycle: what changes in practice
When a foreigner receives a B permit for the Canton of Aargau, they acquire the legal right to reside and work in the Swiss territory for the period indicated on the document. This right is subject to the maintenance of the conditions that led to the issuance: job stability, absence of criminal convictions, and payment of the prescribed social contributions (AVS/AI/IPG, LAMAL, and other contributions depending on the employment situation).
A significant difference between the B permit and other permits concerns the renewal procedure. In the case of the L permit, the short-term resident does not have the right to automatic renewal; they must instead apply for a new permit if they wish to stay. In the case of the B permit, however, renewal is an ordinary procedure that presupposes the continuation of the same working and social conditions. If the resident has maintained employment, paid taxes regularly, and has not violated criminal or civil norms, renewal is generally granted.
### Tax and social security implications
Anyone holding a B permit in the Canton of Aargau is required to pay federal, cantonal, and communal taxes, as well as all mandatory social contributions. Aargau's taxation follows the Swiss three-tier system: direct federal tax managed by the Federal Customs Administration (AFC), cantonal tax managed by the cantonal administration, and communal tax based on the communal multiplier applied to the cantonal rate.
Regarding social security, the resident with a B permit is compulsorily enrolled in AVS/AI (old-age and disability insurance), the IPG contribution (loss of earnings tax), and the mandatory unemployment insurance (AD) up to the annual maximum. If the person is employed, the employer pays the federal contribution equal to 10.6% of the gross salary (5.3% at the employee's expense and 5.3% at the company's expense), plus the amount necessary for unemployment insurance and accident insurance.
### Expiry and renewal: critical timelines
It is crucial to submit the renewal request BEFORE the expiry of the current permit. If the permit expires without a requested renewal, the resident loses the legality of residence and work. The Aargau cantonal migration office is the authority responsible for examining the renewal request and its approval. The documents to be produced and the exact timelines remain to be verified with the competent office, as they vary according to the specific cantonal procedures and the personal situation of the applicant.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to proceed: step-by-step towards renewal
For those in the Canton of Aargau with a B permit nearing expiration, the renewal procedure begins by contacting the cantonal migration office. This is the competent authority for the entire administrative procedure in the canton. It is advisable to submit the request at least 2-3 months before the expiration date to allow the office time to process the application and request any additional documents.
The required documents for renewal will vary depending on the individual situation: current employment contract, tax return, certificate of good conduct (if required), proof of tax and contribution payments, and in some cases, proof of accommodation. The cantonal office will communicate the exact list of required documents during the procedure.
### Implications for workers and residents
Those legally residing in the Canton of Aargau with a B permit have the same rights and obligations as Swiss residents in terms of contributions and taxes. This means full payment of income tax, wealth tax (if applicable in the canton), and capital tax, as well as contributions to social security (AHV/IV/EO, AD, AC, LAMal). At the same time, they accumulate pension rights: each year of AHV contributions counts towards future pensions.
Regarding mandatory health insurance (LAMal), anyone legally residing in Switzerland must take out insurance within 3 months of arrival. The insurance is private, with per capita premiums varying by canton and region of residence. In the Canton of Aargau, premiums may benefit from cantonal subsidies for premium reduction (premium subsidy) for those falling under certain income thresholds.
### Additional resources and information
To verify the complete list of documents required for renewal in the Canton of Aargau and the exact deadlines, it is essential to contact the cantonal migration office directly. Information published by the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) at the federal level provides the general framework, but the specific procedural details remain the competence of the canton. The State Secretariat for Migration publishes official guides on permits and procedures; the website of the Aargau cantonal administration contains additional information on processing times and deadlines.
If doubts arise during the renewal process regarding tax or pension status, it is possible to consult the cantonal or federal tax administration. Similarly, for clarifications on pension rights and obligations, the Federal Social Insurance Office (FSIO) provides detailed information on AHV, disability, unemployment, and supplementary insurances.

item.title: Opening businesses in Basel Countryside: registers and costs
item.description: Registration in the commercial register, legal forms, social security and insurance obligations: everything you need to start a business in the canton.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Registration with the cantonal commercial register is mandatory for every new business - Three levels of taxation: federal, cantonal, and municipal - Pension obligations: AHV/AI, BVG, KVG, accident insurance (UVG)
## Key facts - **What**: Opening a business with registration in the cantonal commercial register - Where: Canton of Basel-Landschaft - Who: Entrepreneurs, self-employed workers, small and medium-sized companies - Levels of taxation: 3 (federal, cantonal, municipal) - AHV/AI contributions: 5.3% from employee, 5.3% from employer (total 10.6%) - BVG contributions: Vary from 7% (25-34 years) to 18% (55+ until reference age) - KVG: Mandatory, deductibles from CHF 300 to CHF 2500 for adults
Starting a business in Switzerland, specifically in the canton of Basel-Landschaft, requires compliance with federal, cantonal, and municipal obligations ranging from registration in the commercial register to pension and tax requirements. Switzerland does not have a centralized business administration model: each canton manages its own commercial register according to common federal principles, but with modalities and deadlines that can vary slightly from territory to territory.
The first mandatory step is registration with the cantonal commercial register. This register is public and tracks all individual businesses, general partnerships, limited partnerships, limited liability companies, and corporations. Without registration, the activity is not legally recognized, and the owner risks administrative penalties. The Swiss tax system is structured in three levels: the federal direct tax (managed by the Federal Customs Administration), cantonal taxes, and municipal taxes (applied as a multiplier on the cantonal tax base). For those exercising an independent commercial or professional activity, taxes are calculated on the net income derived from accounting.
But taxation is only part of the obligations. Those who open a business with employees must immediately register themselves and their collaborators in the federal social security system. This means affiliation with AHV/AI with contributions of 5.3% for the employee and 5.3% for the employer (total 10.6% on gross salary). If the income from independent activity exceeds federal thresholds, the obligation to register with the BVG (professional pension fund) is triggered, with contributions ranging from 7% in the 25-34 age group to 18% for collaborators over 55 until the reference age.
Those who hire employees must also pay unemployment contributions (AL, 1.1% up to the annual maximum) and accident insurance (UVG, 0.7-1.5% depending on the sector of activity). Health insurance (KVG) is mandatory for all residents in Switzerland, regardless of professional status, and provides deductibles from CHF 300 to CHF 2500 for adults based on the customer's choice. Consult our health insurance comparison tool to navigate the available options in the canton.
### Choosing the legal form
The legal form significantly impacts personal liability, accounting obligations, and tax burden. An individual business entails unlimited liability of the owner to creditors but is the simplest form administratively and does not require a minimum paid-in capital. A limited liability company requires minimum capital and entails liability limited to the paid-in capital. A corporation is suitable for larger businesses and requires significant capital. The choice of legal form must also consider accounting obligations, the desired liability regime, and the expected tax burden. Each legal form has different implications on the three levels of taxation and registration with the cantonal office.
### The costs and tax levels
Anyone starting a business in Switzerland faces a tax structure with three levels, each managed by different authorities. At the federal level, the Federal Customs and Tax Administration collects the federal direct tax, calculated as a percentage of the net income of the business. Income is also subject to value-added tax (VAT), a federal tax on turnover, if the annual turnover exceeds certain federal registration thresholds.
At the cantonal level, the canton of Basel-Landschaft applies its own direct tax rate according to its tax legislation. At the municipal level, the municipalities of the canton apply a multiplier to the cantonal tax base, which means that two different municipalities in the same canton can have slightly different taxes. The exact amount of municipal tax therefore varies depending on whether the business is located in Liestal, Waldenburg, Buckten, or other municipalities of Basel-Landschaft. This system allows municipalities to have some fiscal autonomy but requires the taxpayer to check the specific rates in the chosen municipality.
### Social security obligations for the owner and employees
If an entrepreneur works alone as a sole proprietor without employees, they are still obliged to pay AVS/AI contributions on a quarterly or annual basis. The rate is 10.6% of net income (the owner pays both the employee and employer portions), up to a federal coordinated income ceiling set and indexed annually.
If the business involves employees, the calculation becomes significantly more complex. For each employee, the employer pays monthly: - 5.3% for AVS/AI - 5.3% for IPG (loss of earnings compensation) - 1.1% for unemployment insurance (AD) up to the annual ceiling - 0.7-1.5% for accident insurance (LAA), depending on the sector of activity
Additionally, if an employee's coordinated salary exceeds the federal threshold for pension fund registration (an annually indexed figure), the employer is obliged to enroll the employee in the LPP/BVG (professional pension fund) system, paying contributions that vary according to the age bracket: 7% (25-34 years), 10% (35-44 years), 15% (45-54 years), 18% (55+ until the reference age). If the salary remains below the coordination threshold, enrollment in the LPP is not mandatory by law, although the employer can offer a voluntary pension solution.
Each employee must also subscribe to private health insurance (LAMal), with deductibles ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2500 according to personal choice. This is a mandatory individual insurance by law, not a salary contribution deducted by the employer. Many employers negotiate collective rates with health insurance companies for their employees, reducing their premium. Learn more about the [supplementary pension system LPP](nav:pension) to better understand the obligations towards employees with high coordinated salaries.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to register a business in Baselland: the step-by-step procedure
The procedure for opening a business follows a standard path throughout Switzerland, with minor variations depending on the canton and the chosen legal form. Here are the concrete steps:
Step 1 – Choose legal form and verify name
Before proceeding, it is essential to define the legal form (sole proprietorship, limited liability company, joint-stock company, cooperative, etc.). Once defined, verify the availability of the name with the cantonal commercial register office of Baselland. The name cannot be identical to already registered businesses in the same canton and must not violate naming regulations. If you choose a form that requires minimum capital (such as a limited liability company), ensure the capital is deposited with a banking institution within the federal deadlines.
Step 2 – Registration with the cantonal commercial register
Contact the commercial register office of the canton of Baselland. You will need to submit: the official registration form (available at the office or online on the cantonal website), identity documents of the owner or legal representative, articles of association and statutes for corporate forms, capital deposit certificate (if required by the legal form), documentation of the business premises (lease agreement, ownership or loan agreement). Once registered, you will receive a business identification number (IDI) assigned by the Federal Statistical Office, similar to a federal business tax code.
Step 3 – Registration with the AVS system and social security
Simultaneously or immediately after registering with the commercial register, register with the competent AVS compensation fund for the canton of Baselland. You will need to declare the estimated net income of the business for the correct payment of contributions. If the income exceeds the federal coordination threshold, you will need to simultaneously subscribe to the pension fund (LPP) with an authorized professional insurance. If you hire employees, register them with the same AVS fund and pay monthly contributions for both AVS/AI and unemployment and accident insurance.
Step 4 – VAT registration (if applicable)
If the estimated turnover exceeds the federal mandatory registration threshold, register for VAT with the federal tax administration (VAT Office). If you remain below the threshold, you can choose voluntary registration to recover VAT on business purchases. This decision has significant tax implications and it is advisable to evaluate it with a professional.
Step 5 – Annual tax obligations and payments
Each year, declare the net income of your business through the federal income tax return (with the Federal Customs Administration) and the cantonal return with the tax administration of Baselland. If you are subject to VAT, you will pay balances periodically based on quarterly or annual declarations according to the chosen regime. If you have employees, you will also need to declare the salaries paid and social contributions annually. Typical deadlines are: VAT declaration every quarter (or year according to the regime), federal and cantonal income tax return by March 31 of the following year, AVS contribution payment by the 5th of the month following the calculation period.
### Essential documents to prepare
For each legal form, previously assemble: valid identity document of the owner, civil registry extract (for sole proprietorships), signed articles of association and statutes (for companies), capital deposit certificate with a Swiss bank (for forms that require it), lease agreement or ownership deed of the business premises. Having these documents ready significantly speeds up the registration process and avoids administrative delays.
Use our [salary and tax calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate in advance the social charges and tax burden of your business. You can model different scenarios of income, number of employees, and legal forms to better understand the actual management costs of your company in the canton of Baselland and in your specific municipality of residence.

## In short - Mandatory registration with the commercial register of the canton - Swiss taxation: 3 levels (federal, cantonal, municipal) - Legal forms: sole proprietorship, simple partnership, SA, SARL - Pension contributions: AVS/AI 5.3%, LAMal, LPP, LAA mandatory
## Key facts - **What**: Opening a business and registering with the commercial register - Where: Canton of Basel-Landschaft (like every Swiss canton) - Who: Individual entrepreneurs, sole proprietorships, companies - Legal forms: Sole proprietorship, simple partnership, SA, SARL - Tax levels: Federal (AFC/ESTV) + cantonal + municipal - Pension: AVS/AI, LAMal, LPP, LAA all mandatory - Competencies: AFC/ESTV manages IFD and VAT; cantonal administrations manage cantonal and municipal taxes
Opening a business in the Canton of Basel-Landschaft requires mandatory registration with the local commercial register. As in every Swiss canton, this procedure represents the first concrete administrative step. The choice of legal form — sole proprietorship, simple partnership, public limited company (SA) or limited liability company (SARL) — determines the tax structure, administrative obligations, and the degree of personal liability of the owner.
### Choosing the legal form: concrete implications
The sole proprietorship is the simplest form: a single natural person exercises the activity under their own name, without constituting a separate legal entity. The owner is unlimitedly liable for commercial obligations with their personal assets. The simple partnership requires at least two partners and maintains a minimal legal structure, suitable for informal partnerships. The public limited company (SA) and the limited liability company (SARL) are forms with their own legal personality and defined share capital. In these forms, partners and managers have limited liability to the capital contributed. The choice directly affects federal, cantonal, and municipal taxation, as well as obligations towards the commercial register and tax authorities.
### Procedure for registration with the commercial register
Each canton manages its own commercial register through specific administrative offices. In the Canton of Basel-Landschaft, as in other cantons, registration is mandatory for all legal forms. The procedure varies slightly between cantons, but the essential elements remain constant. The required documentation typically includes: identification of the owner (identity document), certificate of residence, copy of the statutes or constitutive act (for companies), declaration of the legal form and operational headquarters. Once registered, the company receives an ISE number (statistical economic identifier) used for federal, cantonal, and municipal tax registrations. The costs and deadlines for registration vary by canton — Basel-Landschaft applies its own amounts and terms. Consult [the site's calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate the initial costs related to your legal form. ### Swiss tax system: three levels of taxation
The Swiss tax system operates simultaneously on three distinct and independent levels: federal, cantonal, and municipal. The federal direct tax (IFD) and the value-added tax (VAT) are administered by the federal authorities (AFC — Federal Customs Administration — and ESTV — Federal Tax Administration). Each canton, including Basel-Landschaft, sets its own cantonal tax rates. Each municipality within the canton applies its own multiplier based on the cantonal rate, thus generating variable municipal taxes. A new company must register with the AFC/ESTV for IFD and VAT at the federal level. Simultaneously, registration with the cantonal authorities of Basel-Landschaft for cantonal taxes and with the municipality of residence/headquarters for municipal taxes is mandatory. This means that the total tax burden depends on both federal rates and the decisions of each specific canton and municipality.
### Pension, health insurance, and accident insurance obligations
Starting a business automatically entails pension and insurance obligations that cannot be overlooked. The Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance (AVS/AI) is mandatory for anyone exercising a gainful activity, including the entrepreneur themselves. If you hire employees, you must register them in the AVS/AI system. The total contribution is calculated based on the salary: the employee pays 5.3% and the employer pays another percentage (the total is 10.6% gross). In addition to AVS/AI, registration with a private health insurance (LAMal) is mandatory within three months of starting the activity. LAMal is not a tax or salary contribution but a private insurance policy with individually variable premiums depending on the canton and region. For employees with a coordinated salary above a specific threshold, registration with a professional pension fund (second pillar, LPP/BVG) is mandatory. LPP contributions vary by age class of the worker: 7% for ages 25-34, 10% for 35-44, 15% for 45-54, and 18% for ages 55 until the reference age. Accident insurance (LAA/UVG) is mandatory for every employee. The employer pays the entire contribution; the rate depends on the sector of activity (from 0.7% to about 1.5%). These obligations are not optional: failure to comply results in administrative and tax penalties.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-step procedure: from idea to operational activity
Step 1: Define the legal form and prepare the documentation — Before officially registering, decide whether to operate as a sole proprietorship (simpler but unlimited liability) or to form a company (SA, SARL, simple company — more complex but separation of personal and business assets). For a sole proprietorship, gather: valid ID, residence certificate, and possibly a criminal record certificate (at the discretion of the canton). For a company, prepare: statutes or articles of association signed by all partners, manager's declaration, and a bank certificate attesting the deposit of the share capital.
Step 2: Register the activity in the cantonal commercial register — Contact the competent office of the Canton of Basel-Landschaft (commercial register office). Submit the complete documentation according to the canton's checklist. The office verifies compliance, registers the company in the public register, and issues a registration certificate. This certificate is essential for subsequent tax registrations.
Step 3: Federal, cantonal, and municipal tax registrations — With the registration certificate, the company automatically receives an ISE (Economic Statistical Identifier). Using this number, apply for registration with the AFC/ESTV for federal direct tax (FDT) and value-added tax (VAT). Simultaneously, register with the tax authorities of the Canton of Basel-Landschaft for cantonal taxes and with the municipality of residence for municipal taxes. Each authority will provide specific taxpayer numbers.
**Step 4: Basic insurances** — Subscribe to private health insurance (LAMal) within three months of starting the activity with a health insurance fund of your choice. If you hire employees, register them immediately in the AVS/AI system with the competent compensation office. If their salary exceeds the coordination threshold, also register them with a chosen LPP fund (second pillar) from the available funds. Subscribe to accident insurance (LAA) with a recognized insurer, providing data on the sector of activity.
Step 5: Check deadlines and annual obligations — After starting, you will need to submit annual tax declarations to the AFC/ESTV (FDT and VAT), to the cantonal authorities of Basel-Landschaft (cantonal taxes), and to the municipality (municipal taxes). Employees require monthly payments of AVS/AI contributions and annual notifications to the compensation office. Health insurance must remain active continuously.
To calculate the initial tax impact and predict the contribution burden on employees, use the [tax calculator](nav:calculator) on the site. To plan long-term retirement and understand the options of the third pillar (3a), consult the [third pillar guide](nav:pillar3). item.title: AVS and Supplementary Benefits in the Canton of Basel-Landschaft
item.description: How the Swiss First Pillar Works in the Cantonal Compensation Fund. AVS Pensions, Contribution Gaps, and Benefits to Ensure a Minimum Standard of Living.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - AVS: 5.3% employee contribution, 10.6% gross (including employer contribution). Forms the basis of the pension system. - Supplemental benefits: supplement insufficient AVS pensions up to the subsistence level. - Compensation fund: Manages contributions and calculates pensions at the cantonal level. - Contribution gaps: Periods without contributions reduce the pension; the system provides for top-up payments.
## Key Facts - **What**: AVS (First Pillar), supplementary benefits, cantonal compensation fund - Where: Canton of Basel-Landschaft (uniform federal procedures across all cantons) - Who: Employees, employers, Swiss residents; administered by the Federal Social Insurance Office (BSV) at the federal level - Contribution: 5.3% employee, 10.6% total (including employer’s share) - Administration: Cantonal administration + cantonal compensation fund
The first pillar of the Swiss pension system, the AVS, forms the foundation of the social security system for those living and working in Switzerland. In the Canton of Basel-Landschaft, as in other cantons, the local compensation fund manages the contributions paid by employees and employers in accordance with uniform federal regulations. Every employed resident pays 5.3% of their gross salary into the AVS (to which the employer adds another 5.3%), accumulating pension rights year after year. Those with contribution gaps—periods without contributions—may be eligible for supplementary benefits to ensure a minimum standard of living in retirement.
Supplementary benefits represent a mechanism of federal solidarity: when a retiree’s AVS pension does not cover essential living expenses (rent, food, healthcare), the government makes up the difference up to a maximum limit. This system is crucial for those with a fragmented work history or who have paid contributions for fewer than 43 years. In the canton of Basel-Landschaft, as throughout Switzerland, the entity responsible for this supplementation is the cantonal administration, which works in coordination with the Federal Social Insurance Office (UFAS/BSV). Those receiving supplementary benefits are also entitled to KVG (health insurance) subsidies: See health insurance options →
### Role of the Cantonal Compensation Office
The Compensation Office of the Canton of Basel-Landschaft is not a bank but a federal administrative office with cantonal-regional jurisdiction. Its main task is to record the AVS contributions paid throughout a person’s working life, verify that payments are complete, and calculate the pension based on the average of the coordinated annual wages. When an employee changes jobs, the new employer reports the contributions to the fund, which updates the individual’s file. At the end of their working career (between the ages of 64 and 70), the retiree submits a pension application to the same fund, which performs the final calculation. The AVS calculation follows federal rules that are identical in all cantons: credits accrue for each year of contributions, while years without contributions are considered gaps. If the gaps exceed certain limits, the monthly pension is reduced proportionally. Supplementary benefits are not an optional additional pension, but a federal legal entitlement recognized by Swiss law. Anyone whose AVS pension falls below the legally defined subsistence minimum (an amount indexed annually, not yet specified here) may apply to the relevant cantonal office. In the canton of Basel-Landschaft, the application is submitted to the cantonal social services office, which assesses income, assets, and personal circumstances. The system takes into account both the AVS pension and other sources of income (rental income, LPP/BVG occupational pensions, third-pillar savings, and family allowances) and supplements them until the minimum cost of living recognized by federal law is covered.
### Scenario: Contribution Gaps and Reduced Pension
A resident who has paid AVS contributions for 35 years (instead of 43) has an 8-year contribution gap. Their AVS pension will be calculated based on 35 years of average earnings, with a proportional reduction compared to a full 43-year career. If this pension is insufficient, supplementary benefits will top it up to the subsistence minimum (the amount varies by canton and family situation; check with your local compensation office). The application for supplementary benefits is submitted to the cantonal administration, not to the AVS fund. Supplementary benefits also take into account Disability Insurance (AI) if the applicant is entitled to it. In the canton of Basel-Landschaft, the same federal rules apply as in all other cantons: the federal agency UFAS/BSV defines the criteria, the cantonal administration manages the cases, and the compensation office provides data on the AVS pension.
### Importance of Contribution Records and Preventive Checks
Anyone who wants to maximize their AVS pension must ensure that every year of employment is correctly recorded by the compensation fund. Before retiring, it is wise to check your AVS statement (available from the fund itself or via the online portal) to verify that no contributions are missing. If there are errors—perhaps due to periods spent abroad, a change in employer, or personal financial difficulties—you can request a supplement or a review from the fund. This check must be done years before retirement, not at the time of applying for the pension. [Approfondisci il calcolo della tua rendita nel nostro calcolatore AVS →](nav:pension)
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to Apply for an AVS Pension and Supplementary Benefits
The process consists of two parallel steps. Step 1: About 1–2 months before turning 65 (for women) or 65 (for men), the employee automatically receives an informational letter and an AVS pension application form from the compensation fund. If you do not receive this letter, contact the compensation fund for the canton of Basel-Landschaft directly. Fill out the form, attach a copy of your passport or ID card, and submit it by mail or in person. Step 2: At the same time, if you anticipate that your AVS pension will be insufficient (e.g., due to gaps in coverage or a fragmented work history), submit a separate application for supplementary benefits to the cantonal social assistance office in Basel-Landschaft. There is no strict deadline for this application, but it is advisable to submit it immediately after receiving the AVS pension calculation from the fund to avoid losing retroactive entitlements.
### Required Documents and Administrative Procedure
For the AVS pension application: the pension fund’s official form, a valid ID, and income statements for the past few years (if necessary). For the application for supplementary benefits: a copy of the AVS calculation letter received from the fund, a detailed list of other income and assets (rental income, bank interest, LPP, family allowances), and a statement of essential monthly expenses (rent, utilities, medical care). If you are a foreign national: proof of residence (C residence permit for Switzerland). All official information and forms are available at the office of the Cantonal Compensation Fund of Basel-Landschaft. Communication between the AVS fund and the supplementary benefits office is coordinated at the federal level, so there is no need to submit duplicate copies of the same documentation. However, always check with your local fund to confirm exactly which documents are required, as cantonal administrative procedures may involve minor additional details.

SBB has drawn irritated reactions from some users with its advice on finding seats on trains. The railway company proposed five tips—including delaying your departure time or reserving a seat for a fee—which some commuters have called “absurd.”
According to SBB data, more than 70% of seats remain empty throughout the day, but most of the demand is concentrated during the morning and evening rush hours. This leads many travelers to feel forced to stand during their commute.
SBB explained that adding cars is not straightforward and outlined the measures taken to increase seating capacity. However, the proposed advice has drawn criticism, with some users calling SBB’s post “passive-aggressive” and the suggested solutions “absurd.”

According to SBB, it is helpful to check the online schedule and crowd forecasts. The app and the new platform displays show occupancy by car. Even on routes indicating high occupancy, there are often empty seats at the front and rear of the train.
